Geometry & precision

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how satellite directions map range noise into position uncertainty.

Linearizing the planar example gives Hᵢ = (−cos αᵢ, −sin αᵢ, 1), with the clock parameter expressed as a distance. For equal independent range errors of standard deviation σ, covariance is σ²(HᵀH)⁻¹ when the geometry has full rank.

Similar source directions produce nearly redundant rows, enlarging uncertainty in weakly constrained combinations of position and clock. The plotted position ellipse comes from the position covariance submatrix with equal spatial scales.

In three-dimensional DOP terminology, PDOP² = HDOP² + VDOP² and GDOP² = PDOP² + TDOP². The planar ellipse here illustrates the mechanism rather than calculating a full three-dimensional GDOP.

Example

For fixed geometry, doubling σ doubles every uncertainty-ellipse axis and multiplies its area by four. Better range precision and better geometry address different factors in the covariance.

    Practice

    1. With geometry unchanged, what happens to the 95% position ellipse if independent ranging standard deviation falls from 4 m to 2 m?

    Covariance scales as σ², while ellipse lengths scale as σ.

    Every ellipse axis halves and its area becomes one quarter. Its orientation and axis ratio remain unchanged.
